investigations.name: adhesion-calibration
investigations.objective: Can the neutral adhesion be lowered so a mechanics-only sheet has comparable cell-shape statistics on both substrates, and is the J<->tension mapping sharply identified?
investigations.claim: REVISED per the 2026-10-27 review: this is NOT a calibration of CPM contact energy J to vertex line tension, and the sheets are NOT established as physically matched. The CPM (23.6 um^2) and vertex (34.9 um^2) mean areas differ by ~48%, and the vertex shape statistics are nearly INSENSITIVE to tension_scale over 0.5..8 -- so tension is weakly/non-identifiable from this test. What this study honestly shows: the neutral adhesion strength lowers DIRECTLY to J and MONOTONICALLY (same sign) to line tension, a DIRECTIONAL relation only. A proper physical-observable calibration (relaxation time, interfacial length, deformation under force, migration mobility, neighbour exchange) with identifiability analysis is deferred to Stage 3 / BP-07.

investigations.name: bp-01-blueprint-schema
investigations.title: BP-01 — the blueprint as a versioned, backend-neutral artifact
investigations.objective: Can the biological blueprint be specified as a versioned, backend-neutral, statically-validated artifact, independent of CPM/vertex implementations?
investigations.claim: Stage 1 / BP-01 of the review program. The canonical blueprint is now a VERSIONED, backend-neutral artifact with a checked contract and a static validator -- the first of the three claims (blueprint fidelity) made a first-class, tested object rather than an implicit input. Specifically: (a) a `blueprint_version` field + versioned JSON schema; (b) a canonical/backend split (CompileOptions) so backend/run parameters (tension_scale, rules_seed) are kept OUT of the canonical biological state and recorded separately; (c) a static validator (`validate_blueprint` + `multicell-blueprint validate`) that reports structured diagnostics (errors AND contract warnings), not a success badge; (d) three hand-authored worked examples that validate and compile identically to BOTH backends.

investigations.name: crossparadigm-equivalence
investigations.title: Backend equivalence (TOST)
investigations.objective: Are CPM and vertex EQUIVALENT (not merely "not-distinguishable") under replication -- and on which outcome: cell fate, exact spatial position, or both?
investigations.claim: SCOPED to Claim 3 (scientific equivalence) — NOT blueprint fidelity, NOT biological validity. On cell FATE the two substrates are equivalent under a DEPENDENCE-AWARE reanalysis: the 6x6 grid's 36 cross + 30 same pairs reuse only 6+6 runs and are statistically dependent, so the unit of resampling is the RUN. A run-cluster percentile bootstrap gives Delta(same-cross) -0.0015, 90% CI [-0.003, +0.001], inside a +/-0.05 margin -- so fate agreement is equivalent. CAVEATS (reviewer): the +/-0.05 margin is NOT yet biologically justified; the tight CI reflects LOW between-run variance at this reduced scale, not strong power. The earlier pair-level TOST (p=5.6e-36) treated dependent pairs as independent and OVERSTATED significance -- retired as the headline. Exact spatial position is NOT equivalent (cross 0.08 vs same 1.00; ~8.5 um median drift; 1.0 at t0) -- a CANDIDATE representation effect (lattice COM vs relaxing polygon centroid), NOT yet causally isolated (BP-02/BP-04 will isolate it).

investigations.name: dose-response-crossparadigm
investigations.objective: Do the two substrates agree on the SIGN of the dose response over initial viral load (more load -> more infection), robustly across seeds?
investigations.claim: Both backends agree on the DIRECTION of the dose response: a HIGHER initial viral load (more initially-infected epithelial cells) ends with STRICTLY more infection than a LOWER load, on every backend and seed tested. This is a directional (lowest-vs-highest) result; intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent and is NOT claimed.

investigations.name: flu-lung-crossparadigm
investigations.objective: Does one backend-neutral blueprint reproduce the Sego 2022 influenza model on two different mechanical substrates, and -- judged against same-backend seed noise -- do the substrates diverge?
investigations.claim: The ONE backend-neutral Sego 2022 influenza blueprint compiles to BOTH the CPM (viva-cpm) and vertex (vivarium-tyssue) substrates and runs the Sego model WITH NAMED DEVIATIONS (V/L/C/F producers absent, latent-pool recruitment approximation) end-to-end on each. Because the field / rules / systemic-ODE / recruitment mechanism is shared byte-for-byte across the two compiles, we test for a substrate effect against a NULL CONTROL (same-backend seed-to-seed spread). On cell fate and infected-patch LOCATION the cross-backend difference sits inside the same-backend seed spread, so at this scale and seed count we FAIL TO REJECT the null (no detectable substrate effect -- NOT proof of equality). The one exception is raw infected-patch occupancy IoU, which trends ~25-35% below both same-backend baselines -- a candidate weak substrate signal to test at larger scale / more vertex seeds.

investigations.name: initial-state-fidelity
investigations.objective: Do both substrates faithfully reproduce the blueprint's initial centroids, sizes and types, and how clean is the vertex 1:1 identity?
investigations.claim: Both backends reproduce the blueprint's t=0 state -- every cell's centroid, size and type -- when the one backend-neutral blueprint is compiled onto each. The CPM side is EXACT (centroid residual 0); the vertex side is within a sub-cell residual (RMS ~1.2 um) and achieves a clean 1:1 identity for every cell (fraction_clean 1.0).

investigations.name: substrate-divergence-counterfactual
investigations.title: Mechanics-dominated counterfactual (positive control)
investigations.objective: When MECHANICS (not the shared mechanism) drives the outcome, does the equivalence test correctly REJECT -- i.e. does it have the power to detect a real substrate difference?
investigations.claim: In a MECHANICS-DOMINATED regime (strong differential adhesion + a strong chemoattractant gradient, no shared rules/ODE), the two substrates DIVERGE: the spatial equivalence test REJECTS equivalence (cross-backend spatial agreement 0.20 vs same-backend 1.00; TOST diff +0.80, margin +/-0.10). The divergence is mechanistically attributable -- the vertex fork's ActiveMigration climbs the gradient (type-A mean y 7 -> 17.9) while CPM's Metropolis chemotaxis barely moves it (y -> 10.7). This is the POSITIVE CONTROL for crossparadigm-equivalence: it proves the equivalence test can detect a real substrate difference, so the equivalence verdict on the Sego model is informative, not an artifact of an insensitive metric.
